decision: Decide whether the ridge-0.1 whitened global read is safe on QM9 and reproducibly improves ATOM3D-LBA ID30 enough to justify conditional mechanism and optimizer follow-ups.

population.qm9: QM9 gap, seeded random-row validation split, small equilibrium molecules
population.lba: ATOM3D LBA official ID30 train/validation, bound protein-pocket/ligand crystal complexes

non_goals: No cold-target, cold-ligand, prospective-screening, or published-model superiority claim
No default change from a one-seed or safety-only result

claims.claim: Ridge 0.1 remains finite on QM9 and changes fixed-budget validation MAE by at most 0.020 eV.
claims.required_support: Paired seed-42 500-update strict-CUDA candidate and whitened records with matched split, base initialization, and closed test.
claims.falsifier: Nonfinite execution, absolute validation-MAE delta above 0.020 eV, split/init mismatch, or test access.
claims.permitted_inference: QM9 numerical safety under this harness only

claims.claim: Ridge 0.1 improves mean paired fixed-budget LBA ID30 validation RMSE by at least 0.020 pK across seeds 41--43.
claims.required_support: Mean improvement >=0.020 pK, at least 2/3 wins, worst regression <=0.050 pK, latency and peak ratios <=1.25, frozen topology, matched updates, and no test access.
claims.permitted_inference: Same-harness ID30 validation improvement; not external generalization

claims.claim: If C-WGR-1 and C-WGR-2 pass, clipping interaction and scalar/vector ablations identify whether the gain is optimization-mediated and which value lane is necessary.
claims.required_support: Predeclared paired follow-up arms with gradient-scale diagnostics and lane isolation.
claims.falsifier: Primary confirmation fails, conditional runs are incomplete, or lane/optimizer effects are inconsistent.
claims.permitted_inference: Mechanism hypothesis inside the same training harness

execution_order: CPU and bounded real-data CUDA smoke
Documentation, provenance, independent review, commit, and push
risks: Repeated use of the same LBA validation split creates adaptive selection bias.
Seeds quantify training variability but are not independent biological samples.
Near-universal clipping can mediate architecture effects through effective update scale.
Long GPU runs must bind to an immutable source commit.
